correctness.rationale: Every species is an edge and remains unobserved iff both endpoints are unselected. Exact one-edge and two-edge inclusion probabilities p2,p3,p4 give the normalized conditional variance. For n>=4 the coefficient p3-p4 is positive exactly for 1<=k<=n-3; k=1 recovers W. Tree degree excesses prove sharp extrema. Exhaustive 2-5 vertex degree classification establishes no smaller ambiguity; explicit six-site forests A/B are connected trees with W=5, identical means/variances, different 15-pair laws; adding leaves to their central site preserves W and changes the probability at R2=2 by 1/binom(n,2) for every n>=6. A packaged exact verifier checked 18,244 labeled trees n4..7 and 2,238,496 site subsets, plus ten infinite-family instances; finite checks corroborate, not replace, the proof.

The sharp six-site information-loss theorem is neither the general Q theorem nor an implication from its distinguishing-power result.

originality.rationale: The claim is carefully delimited to the sharp minimal six-site loss of full rarefaction-law information by complete first-two-moment curves, with an all-orders construction. Ugland covers unrestricted conditional moments; Ferrer-i-Cancho covers tree degree extrema; Tittmann et al. covers a stronger full component polynomial but not low-moment injectivity. These covered components are not independently claimed new. Checked primary full texts and searched records do not provide the six-site cutoff or all-orders ambiguity. Remaining unindexed/general-polynomial coverage risk explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Generalized graph-statistic identities could imply some constituent formulas from broader published results not found in the checked sources.
An unindexed study may already tabulate six-site induced edge-count moment coincidences; a negative search does not prove worldwide novelty.
The tree-degree variance extrema are classical and not claimed independently original. Mathematical value hinges on the complete ecological conditional-moment information boundary.
Generality is restricted to minimally connected two-site-species incidence; real habitat incidences commonly violate this constraint.

value.rationale: The minimum six-site ambiguous pair and its all-size continuation identify a precise blind spot of mean-variance sample-based biodiversity accumulation, even with connectivity, uniform occupancy per species, and an exactly fixed interaction budget. For n<=5 such statistics recover the incidence-tree isomorphism type; from n=6, structurally different communities can have identical full mean-and-variance curves but different probabilities of observing a particular richness. This is a motivated, sharp inferential boundary with explicit distributional consequence, not an arbitrary unmotivated finite instance. The classical degree inequalities provide contextual variance bounds rather than serving as the value rationale.
